system_overview: This specification models a trivial PlusCal algorithm that computes the sum of all elements in a sequence of integers, together with its complete machine-checked proof of correctness. It is one of the examples from Section 7.3 of 'Proving Safety Properties' by Leslie Lamport. The algorithm iterates through a sequence from the first element to the last, accumulating a running sum, and terminates when it has processed all elements.
actors_and_components: The system is a single sequential algorithm. There is one actor: the summation procedure, which iterates through a sequence of integers. No concurrency or multiple processes are involved.
state_variables: The system maintains: (1) a sequence of integers drawn from a specified set of integer values, (2) a running sum accumulator, (3) a loop index tracking the current position in the sequence, and (4) a program counter tracking whether the algorithm is still running or has terminated.
initial_state: The sequence is chosen nondeterministically from all sequences of integers drawn from the specified value set (including the empty sequence). The running sum is initialized to zero. The loop index is initialized to 1. The program counter is set to the main loop label.
actions: The algorithm has one main action corresponding to one iteration of the summation loop: (1) If the loop index does not exceed the length of the sequence, add the element at the current index to the running sum and increment the index. (2) If the loop index exceeds the length, the algorithm terminates. The sequence itself remains unchanged throughout execution. A stuttering step is included to prevent deadlock after termination.
safety_properties: Partial correctness: when the algorithm terminates, the running sum equals the sum of all elements in the sequence. This is expressed as an invariant: the postcondition holds whenever the program counter indicates termination. An inductive invariant is defined that tracks the partial sum of elements processed so far.
liveness_properties: Termination: the algorithm eventually reaches its terminal state. This is ensured by weak fairness on the transition relation.
model_bounds: The set of allowed integer values is declared as a constant that must be a subset of the integers. For model checking, the sequence operator would need to be overridden to produce only sequences up to a bounded length.
additional_assumptions: The set of values is assumed to be a subset of the integers. The sum operator on sequences is defined recursively via a tail-inductive function. The proof of correctness is non-trivial because the recursive sum definition processes elements from left to right (starting from the first element) while the algorithm accumulates from right to left (starting from the last element). The proof uses induction to show these two orderings produce the same result. The specification includes a complete TLAPS-checked proof.
